title: Knowledge Distillation with Temperature: Soft Targets and the T² Factor
purpose: Explain how a teacher's logits are turned into soft targets by a temperature-scaled softmax, how the student's soft-target cross-entropy is computed, and why the soft-loss term is multiplied by T² when combined with a hard-label loss.
scope: A single transfer case with small fixed teacher and student logit vectors. We compute the temperature-scaled softmax distributions, the soft-target cross-entropy component, and the T²-scaled combination with a hard-label cross-entropy. No model training, no gradient derivation, no multi-example averaging.
intuition: A high softmax temperature flattens the teacher's distribution, exposing relative preferences among non-target classes that a hard label hides. The student is trained to match this soft distribution. Because raising T shrinks the soft-loss gradients by roughly 1/T², the soft term is multiplied by T² so that its influence relative to the hard-label term stays comparable when T is changed.
learning_objectives: Compute teacher and student softmax distributions at a chosen temperature T and interpret how T controls their sharpness.
Compute the soft-target cross-entropy H(p_T, q_T) and the T²-scaled combination with a hard-label cross-entropy.
prerequisites: Softmax as a normalized exponential of logits.
Cross-entropy H(p,q) = -Σ p_i ln q_i in nats.
assumptions: One transfer case is shown; the paper averages such per-case losses over the transfer set.
The hard-label distribution is a one-hot vector over the same class index used for the teacher's target class.
limitations: We compute the loss components, not the gradients dC/dz_i; the 1/T² gradient scaling is cited but not derived here.
The T² factor is applied as a fixed multiplier on the soft cross-entropy term; the paper's argument is about gradient magnitudes, and we do not re-derive it from the gradient expression.
misconception: That temperature changes the teacher's knowledge or the class ranking. Temperature only rescales logits before softmax; it changes the sharpness of the distribution, not the ordering of classes.
edge_cases: T = 1 makes the soft distribution equal to the ordinary softmax and removes the T² rescaling effect (T² = 1).
A very large T drives both distributions toward uniform, so the soft cross-entropy approaches ln(K) and carries little class-specific signal.

inputs.name: teacher_logits
inputs.label: v (teacher logits)
inputs.meaning: Logits of the cumbersome teacher model for one transfer case.

inputs.name: student_logits
inputs.label: z (student logits)
inputs.meaning: Logits of the distilled student model for the same transfer case.

inputs.name: temperature
inputs.label: T
inputs.meaning: Softmax temperature used both to generate the teacher's soft targets and to train the student.

inputs.name: hard_target
inputs.label: y (hard label)
inputs.meaning: One-hot correct-label distribution over the same classes, used for the hard cross-entropy at T = 1.

inputs.name: hard_weight
inputs.label: α (hard-loss weight)
inputs.meaning: Weight on the hard-label cross-entropy relative to the T²-scaled soft-target term.

steps.name: teacher_soft
steps.label: p (teacher soft targets)
steps.meaning: Teacher logits divided by T, then softmaxed, giving the soft target distribution p_i = e^{v_i/T} / Σ_j e^{v_j/T}.

steps.name: student_soft
steps.label: q (student soft predictions)
steps.meaning: Student logits divided by the same T, then softmaxed, giving q_i = e^{z_i/T} / Σ_j e^{z_j/T}.

steps.name: soft_ce
steps.label: H(p, q)
steps.meaning: Soft-target cross-entropy H(p,q) = -Σ_i p_i ln q_i in nats, computed at the same temperature T used to make the soft targets.

steps.name: student_hard
steps.label: q^(1) (student at T = 1)
steps.meaning: The same student logits softmaxed at temperature 1, as used for the hard-label cross-entropy.

steps.name: hard_ce
steps.label: H(y, q^(1))
steps.meaning: Hard-label cross-entropy H(y, q^(1)) = -Σ_i y_i ln q_i^(1) in nats, computed at temperature 1.

steps.name: combined_loss
steps.label: L
steps.meaning: Weighted combination: the soft-target cross-entropy is multiplied by T² to compensate the 1/T² gradient scaling, and the hard-label cross-entropy is weighted by α.

visuals.question: How does raising T flatten the teacher's soft target distribution p compared with the student's q?
How do the T²-scaled soft term and the α-weighted hard term contribute to the combined loss as T changes?

explorations.title: Low temperature sharpens the soft targets
explorations.observe: At T = 1 the teacher soft distribution is close to the ordinary softmax of v, concentrating mass on the top class, and the T² factor is 1.
explorations.why: Dividing logits by a smaller T preserves larger gaps between logits, so the softmax is sharper; the soft cross-entropy then depends mostly on the top class, and the T² rescaling is inactive.

explorations.title: High temperature softens the targets and amplifies the soft term
explorations.observe: At T = 6 the teacher and student distributions are much closer to uniform, the soft cross-entropy changes, and the T² multiplier (36) makes the soft term dominate the combined loss unless α is large.
explorations.why: Dividing logits by a large T compresses their differences, so softmax approaches uniform and the soft targets carry less class-specific signal; the T² factor grows quadratically, compensating the 1/T² gradient scaling so the soft term's relative influence stays comparable when T is tuned.
